title: Exact completed realization and its normalized derived cohomology comparisons
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $(A,I)$ an adic coefficient datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], in particular $A$ is commutative Noetherian. On the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] write $B_T=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}\underline{A/I^n}$, where $\underline M$ denotes the sheafification of the constant module presheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let $A_T=\varprojlim_n(A/I^n)_T$ be the completed coefficient sheaf of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], and $\gamma:B_T\xrightarrow{\sim}A_T$ the normalized completed coefficient isomorphism used in [def-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-models], induced levelwise by the sheafified constant-function maps $\underline{A/I^n}\to(A/I^n)_T$. Let $F_T:\operatorname{Mod}(A)\to\operatorname{Mod}(A_T)$ be $M\mapsto B_T\otimes_{\underline A}\underline M$, regarded as an $A_T$-module by restriction of scalars along $\gamma^{-1}$; this is the realization of that definition. Then $F_T$ is additive and exact. Its termwise action descends to an exact functor $DF_T:D(A)\to D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_T))$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. There are isomorphisms, natural in $P\in D(A)$ and $M\in\operatorname{Mod}(A)$,
$$F_T(H^q(P))\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(DF_T(P)),\qquad DF_T(M[r])\xrightarrow{\sim}F_T(M)[r]\quad(q,r\in\mathbf Z),$$
where $M[r]$ is the shift of the degree-zero complex. The comparisons are the ones induced by preservation of kernels, images and cokernels on complexes, and by the localization factorization of the termwise functor, followed by exact restriction along the normalized coefficient-ring isomorphism. They hold for unbounded $P$ and arbitrary $M$.

source.place: Tags 093J (lemma-constant-exact), 093M (lemma-completion-flat); derived.tex, Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor). Applied to Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 6.6.11 and Proposition 6.8.11(3); normalized realization is the one in the existing DAG definition.

proof.text: Write $c(M)=\underline M$ for constant module sheafification. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-constant-exact], $c$ preserves finite limits and finite colimits on all $A$-modules, not just finitely presented ones. The site is the small skeleton specified in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], so its smallness hypothesis applies. The explicit functor of [def-sf-site-constant-module-functor] is additive: the map of constant presheaves induced by $f+g$ is the sum of those induced by $f,g$, and this equality persists after sheafification. Thus a short exact sequence of $A$-modules gives a short exact sequence of $\underline A$-module sheaves.

By [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction], $B_T=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}\underline{A/I^n}$ is flat over $\underline A$: tensoring with it preserves every short exact sequence of $\underline A$-module sheaves. Its hypotheses hold because the adic datum makes $A$ commutative Noetherian; no finiteness condition is imposed on $M$. Apply it to the sequence in step 1. Tensoring is additive, since on local tensor generators $(1\otimes(f+g))(b\otimes m)=b\otimes f(m)+b\otimes g(m)$, and these equalities pass to the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The map $\gamma$ is invertible: the adic datum makes every $A/I^n$ finite, so by the last clause of [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction] each levelwise sheafified constant-function map $\underline{A/I^n}\to(A/I^n)_T$ is an isomorphism compatible with the transitions, and $\gamma$ is their limit, with inverse the limit of the inverses. Finally restrict scalars along the specified $\gamma^{-1}:A_T\to B_T$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. This has inverse restriction along $\gamma$; the composites have exactly the original scalar actions. Kernels are sectionwise and cokernels are sheafified sectionwise cokernels in the module categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Neither construction changes under this invertible relabelling of scalars. Hence this restriction is additive and exact, and their composite is exactly the stated $F_T$. Being additive and preserving short exact sequences, $F_T$ preserves kernels and cokernels, hence finite limits and finite colimits (Homology, Tag 010N).

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to the additive exact functor $F_T$ just proved. Its termwise functor $C(F_T)$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms and factors through localization as $DF_T$, with natural isomorphism $\varphi_K:DF_T(Q_AK)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_T(C(F_T)K)$. The same cited statement supplies its shift comparisons and says that this is a triangulated functor, hence exact as a functor of derived categories. This construction uses the unbounded categories throughout; no resolution, convergence assertion or cohomological bound is needed.

For each integer $q$ and each cochain complex $K$, [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] gives $c_K^q:H^q(C(F_T)K)\xrightarrow{\sim}F_T(H^qK)$, induced by the canonical kernel and image comparisons and the resulting quotient comparison. Invert this map and follow it by $H^q(\varphi_K)^{-1}$ to obtain $F_T(H^q(Q_AK))\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(DF_T(Q_AK))$, using the cohomology identification of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. All these maps are natural in chain maps. Both functors on complexes invert quasi-isomorphisms: cohomology does so by definition, $F_T$ preserves isomorphisms, and $C(F_T)$ does so by step 3. Part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] therefore descends this natural isomorphism uniquely to $P\in D(A)$, with its inverse descending as well. This is the requested cohomology comparison, and its construction fixes its normalization. In particular $F_T$ includes scalar restriction along the specified $\gamma^{-1}$; restriction leaves the underlying cycle, boundary and quotient maps unchanged, so this comparison has exactly the prescribed coefficient transport.

source.place: Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor), proof, with the cohomology calculation of homology.tex Tag 010N (lemma-exact-functor); localization as in Tag 05RU (definition-unbounded-derived-category).

proof.text: Let $M[0]$ be the complex with $M$ in degree zero and zero elsewhere. Its termwise image under $F_T$ has $F_T(M)$ in degree zero and zero elsewhere, with zero differentials. Thus $\varphi_{M[0]}$ identifies $DF_T(M[0])$ with $F_T(M)[0]$, naturally in every module map. For $r\in\mathbf Z$, compose the shift comparison from [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] with this degree-zero identification shifted by $r$. This gives $DF_T(M[r])\xrightarrow{\sim}F_T(M)[r]$. At the complex level its map is the identity in each degree: the only possibly nonzero term is $F_T(M)$ in degree $-r$, and every differential is zero. The cited factorization's shift-compatibility equation identifies this with the localization comparison for the shifted complex itself. Consequently the comparison is the specified one, natural in arbitrary $M$, for positive, zero and negative shifts alike.
